Legal working hour limits

RuleSaudi ArabiaUAE
Normal hours8 a day or 48 a week8 a day or 48 a week
Ramadan6 a day and 36 a week for MuslimsTwo hours less a day
BreakAt least half an hour after 5 consecutive hours, not counted as workAt least one hour after 5 consecutive hours
Daily attendance12 hours at most at the workplace—
Overtime limit720 hours a year unless the worker agrees to moreTwo hours a day, and 144 working hours every 3 weeks
Overtime payActual wage + 50% of basicBasic + 25% (50% at night)

Examples:
8 am to 6 pm with a one-hour break, 5 days: 9 hours a day and 45 a week. On the daily standard that is 5 overtime hours a week; on the weekly standard there is no overtime because 45 is under 48.
In Ramadan in Saudi Arabia, 7 actual hours on 5 days is 35 hours, under 36, but each day is one hour over 6 on the daily standard.

To price the overtime in riyals or dirhams, use the Saudi overtime calculator or the UAE overtime calculator. Prefer Arabic? Use the Arabic version.

Frequently asked questions

What are the official working hours in the private sector?

In Saudi Arabia and the UAE, 8 hours a day or 48 hours a week. The employer may use the daily or the weekly standard; under the weekly standard the 48 hours can be spread over the week as long as break and attendance limits are respected.

Do breaks count as working hours?

No. In Saudi Arabia rest periods are not part of actual working hours (Article 102); no one may work more than 5 hours in a row without a break of at least half an hour, or stay at work more than 12 hours a day. In the UAE, a break of at least one hour is due after 5 consecutive hours.

What are the working hours in Ramadan?

In Saudi Arabia, 6 hours a day and 36 a week for Muslim workers. In the UAE, private-sector working hours are reduced by two hours a day during Ramadan.

What is the maximum overtime?

In the UAE, overtime may not exceed two hours a day, and total working hours may not exceed 144 every 3 weeks except to prevent serious loss or an accident. In Saudi Arabia there is an annual cap of 720 overtime hours unless the worker agrees to more.

How is overtime paid?

In Saudi Arabia, the actual hourly wage plus 50% of the basic hourly wage; in the UAE, the basic hourly wage plus 25%, or 50% between 10 pm and 4 am. Work it out in the overtime calculators for the two countries.
